judy-chu.text: Voted No on H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (motion to concur in Senate amendment), July 3, 2025; the bill passed 218-214.
Voted Nay on H.R. 28, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act, January 14, 2025; the bill passed 218-206.
Voted Nay on H. Res. 53, the rule providing for consideration of the Laken Riley Act (S. 5) and the Fix Our Forests Act, January 22, 2025.
Voted Nay on H.R. 1526, the No Rogue Rulings Act, April 9, 2025; the bill passed 219-213.
"I am committed to taking aggressive action to halt and reverse the effects of climate change." Her issues page also stresses ending fossil fuel reliance and investing in clean energy.

Voted against several 2025 measures the League of Conservation Voters scored as anti-environment, including rolling back the methane polluter fee and undermining Endangered Species Act protections. LCV gives her a 97% score for 2025.

source.title: League of Conservation Voters – Judy M. Chu scorecard

judy-chu.text: "Immigration is core to America's strength and has been since our founding." She advocates reforming the broken system and creating pathways for undocumented immigrants.
Her campaign press page opposes Republican Medicaid and ACA cuts, with the headline "GOP's $1.5 Trillion Healthcare Cuts Put Millions at Risk."
Her issues page says she champions heat safety standards for workers and opposes union-busting tax deductions (campaign press page). She also names protecting Social Security as a priority.
Co-introduced the Language Access to Gun Violence Prevention Strategies Act after the Monterey Park shooting.
Co-introduced the PRIDE Act to eliminate gendered language in the tax code; her campaign also highlights her fight to restore reproductive freedoms.
Says she prioritizes "a transportation system that will ease our impact on the environment" and improved regional mobility options.
Says she works to "end all forms of government-sanctioned discrimination" and to protect civil and voting rights.

april-a-verlato.text: Says she supports "legislation aimed at controlling mandatory spending and opposing tax increases" and backs Prop 13 provisions; describes herself as a proponent of the Taxpayer Protection Pledge.
Wants "an economy that thrives on innovation and hard work, not on burdensome regulations that stifle growth."

On homelessness, pursues "strategies that address both its symptoms and root causes," including mental health and substance abuse treatment facilities, reduced bureaucratic delays, and local housing solutions.
Supports stronger border security, calling it "the government's duty to protect its citizens from various threats, including illegal drug trafficking and terrorism."
As an Arcadia council member she voted each year to support the Police Chief's plans and budget requests, and helped organize support for a lawsuit against zero-bail policy.
Campaign platform lists "unwavering support for law enforcement" and "championing market-driven healthcare solutions" among its pillars.
Supports "enhancing America's military strength and ensuring energy independence" and more veterans' care, including more veteran clinics and a major medical center in the San Gabriel Valley.
Advocates "responsible budgeting, targeted spending reviews, and bipartisan collaboration" on the national debt, citing a cut in Arcadia's pension liability from $150 million to under $30 million.

notes: Chu: 2025 House roll-call votes read from clerk.house.gov plus campaign/issues pages; no endorsements recorded (Verlato's site endorsements page was not retrievable, and congress.gov/govtrack/Ballotpedia fetches failed). Verlato has no federal voting record; evidence is her campaign issues page and Arcadia council actions. Her housing, renters, education, guns, social-issues and elections positions were not found.
